thread.title: Mom writes book for daughter's wedding
thread.title_full: Mom writes book for daughter's wedding

author: ohtadmin
title: Mom writes book for daughter's wedding
text:
Jean MacGregor Brown had a special gift for her daughter, Jess, on her wedding day. It was a picture book about her childhood squirrel friend.
Brown presented “Alfred Finds a Very Best Friend” to Jess at her June 15 wedding as she was being married to her husband, Alex Jordan.
After the vows, while everyone was dancing to the music of Dire Straits, Brown called her daughter to the stage. She asked Jess if there were any other animals she was fond of as a child, aside from their dogs. When Jess recalled Alfred, a squirrel she befriended in the family’s window box, Jean gave her the newly completed book as a wedding present.
“She was in shock,” Brown said. “She couldn’t believe I did that.”
“I was completely surprised and in awe of my mom,” Jess said. “While helping me prepare for my wedding, she was also quietly creating this beautiful story inspired by such a special part of my childhood. Alfred brought so much joy to our house growing up, and I’m incredibly grateful that my mom found a way to share that joy with others through this book.”
“Alfred Finds a Very Best Friend” was written by Brown with illustrations from Chris Bonner. She is planning to publish the book for sale later this year. The book tells the true story of how Jess befriended a squirrel she named Alfred in their North End backyard when she was a child. The character based on Jess is called Palmer in the book.
The inspiration for the story came when Brown realized her daughter, as an adult, still remembered Alfred. While Jess was driving about a year ago, a squirrel ran in front of her car. She was worried she might have run over Alfred.
“I realized that this squirrel was really a major part of her life,” Brown said.
Brown, a Vietnam veteran with the U.S. Air Force, has lived in Jamestown since the 1990s. She was a television reporter for WLNE Channel 6 and host of the “Rhode Island Weekly” cable show. She married her husband, Stephen Brown, who was the publisher of The Providence Phoenix alternative weekly newspaper, in 1991. They remained married until his death in 2016. Jess is their only child.
Before the family moved downtown, Brown recalls her daughter playing with squirrels and their dogs as a child in the North End. Jess first met the squirrel through a window box in their living room that was designed with birds in mind.
There was no one specific squirrel that was “Alfred,” something Brown observed when Jess thought the squirrel “moved” with them to their new home.
Brown thought it was important to document her daughter’s relationship with the squirrels. The idea to specifically document it through a book came as Jess was about to get married, and she started writing it in October.
“I thought this would be a good present, because she always said to me ‘You need to write a book,’” Brown said. “I thought to myself, ‘This is what I have to write.’”
When Brown started the book, she began with the true story of how her daughter met the squirrel and how the family’s life was at the time. She included memories like the family dancing to rock music, including Dire Straits.
“It was just such an amazing part of my daughter’s childhood,” Brown said. “I really thought It was important to put it all together.”
Bonner, who lives in San Diego and is a teacher and artist, is Brown’s niece’s son. He’s always drawn as a hobby, but he has started to take it more seriously the last few years and has taken classes.
Brown outlined the story and Bonner painted the pictures. She then revised the story to work better with his art.
“It started with what I originally thought the book would be, and after I saw his pictures, I wrote more to the pictures,” Brown said.
To make his artwork, Bonner said that he drew “a bunch” of sketches of squirrels to get the design of Alfred, and also worked from reference photographs of the family and Rhode Island. Bonner chose an opaque watercolor wash as his medium of choice because it was colorful and produced art that looked like a children’s book. He also drew in pen as a supplemental style to add variety and different color schemes to the book.
Brown said the method of sending pictures and words back and forth “made a lot of sense” during their collaboration. The process took about six months.
Although the book has been presented to its planned recipient, Brown still is working on “Alfred Finds a Very Best Friend” for publication. Her favorite part was seeing the finished copy and Bonner’s depiction of the Newport Pell Bridge on the cover. She noted that her daughter’s friends’ children adore the book.
Brown plans for the book to be available to purchase on Amazon by Labor Day. She also is considering recording an audiobook so children who are blind also can enjoy Alfred’s adventures.

The book tells the true story of how Jess befriended a squirrel she named Alfred in their North End backyard when she was a child. “I thought to myself, ‘This is what I have to write.’” When Brown started the book, she began with the true story of how her daughter met the squirrel and how the family’s life was at the time.
